inbox.text:
Implement a runnable headless TaskChain prototype in Python (adapted from MARBLE coding task 46). No imports, network, filesystem access or main block. Define class TaskChain with:
add_task(task_id, dependencies=None): unique IDs; dependencies must already exist; initially pending. Invalid IDs/dependencies raise ValueError/KeyError without mutation.
start(task_id): pending -> in_progress only when all dependencies completed; otherwise ValueError/KeyError.
complete(task_id): in_progress -> completed only; repeated/invalid transitions raise ValueError/KeyError without mutation or duplicate notifications.
add_comment(task_id, author, text): append {author,text} in order for collaborative notes.
snapshot(): dict keyed by ID, each value {status,dependencies,comments}.
notifications(): list of {kind,task_id}. Completion emits kind=completed; when completion makes a pending dependent runnable, emit kind=ready exactly once. For dependencies [A,C], no ready event before both complete.
report(): dict with sorted ID lists keyed pending,in_progress,completed.
diagram(): Mermaid string containing graph TD or flowchart TD and lines like A --> B for dependencies.
Do not implement a web frontend or claim a full upstream benchmark pass. Perform this task yourself. Call codemode once with source_message_id for this task and a script awaiting tools.submit_taskchain({code:<your Python source>}); print its result with text(). The host supplies message_id. Do not wrap in start_job. The real Python test process may pause until independent task B is finished. A running cell receipt is not completion; never rerun the script to obtain output. End your turn while waiting. When completion arrives, collect the saved full final result with codemode_read; if done=false, follow next_offset. Only after all 12 tests pass and the full result is read, use send_message exactly READY TaskChain/solution.py, replying to this task. No acknowledgements, polling or delegation.
